pages.text: Each layer takes time off every recipe. At the maximum height of 10 a recipe takes $(item)half$() its base time. With the default settings:$(br2)$(item)time = base x (1 - height / 20)$()

$(l)One crushed raw iron (144 mB)$()$(li)$(item)3 layers$(): 340 ticks (17 s)$(li)$(item)4 layers$(): 320 ticks (16 s)$(li)$(item)5 layers$(): 300 ticks (15 s)$(li)$(item)6 layers$(): 280 ticks (14 s)$(li)$(item)8 layers$(): 240 ticks (12 s)$(li)$(item)10 layers$(): 200 ticks (10 s)$(br2)A $(item)reinforced$() furnace halves these times again: 170 ticks at 3 layers, $(item)100 ticks$() at 10.

Hot air is drawn $(item)per tick of work$(), so a faster furnace uses less hot air and less coke per ingot: about 6800 mB of hot air per ingot at 3 layers, 2000 mB at 10 reinforced layers.$(br2)The furnace only counts complete layers, so extra half-built walls on top do nothing.
